notes:
Honda and Acura cars that use 29-bit CAN on the OBD-II socket (ELM327 protocol 7, 500 kbit/s): Civic, Jazz (Fit), CR-V, HR-V, Accord and the Acura Integra, RDX and TLX, as the two sources list them, with UDS service 22. A unit's request identifier is 18DAxxF1 (xx the unit, F1 the tester) and its reply comes from 18DAF1xx.

Every row is an address pair and nothing more: no data identifier or scaling is shipped, because the only sources are other projects' signal definitions, which this repository does not copy. OBDb writes a unit as DAxx, which this profile reads as 18DAxxF1: its schema does not say so, and it rests on opendbc using the full form for the same units. Where the two sources differ: OBDb marks 0x28 as ABS and also lists 0x2A as ABS, while opendbc has only 0x28 (as vsa); OBDb has rows opendbc does not (0x0E, 0x11, 0x1D, 0x26, 0x2A, 0x01), and opendbc has units OBDb does not (0x0B, 0x2B, 0x61, 0xEF, 0xB0, 0xB5, the forward camera and radar). opendbc's 0x10 and 0x60 are listed as extra units its query software probes, not fingerprint units. OBDb's DBEF rows have no reply identifier and one Clarity-only pair of battery units (DA15, DA16) rests on one repository, so those are left out.

opendbc lists a European CR-V and a Civic diesel among its cars, but most of what both sources describe is sold in North America and Japan. A UK or European Honda may lay its units out differently, with some units absent or on another identifier, and the 29-bit scheme may not be on the OBD-II socket at all behind a gateway. opendbc's queries come from a comma.ai device wired into the car, which is not the OBD-II socket. opendbc's own comment says the forward camera does not support being queried in parallel with another unit and that the radar at 18DAB0F1 often fails to respond. Treat every row as unconfirmed until `obd-read probe` shows it answering. The default session, which every UDS unit must accept, is the one opened.

description: Honda and Acura cars with 29-bit CAN addressing (18DAxxF1), UDS service 22

engine-0e.source: OBDb signal set, header DA0E and replies from 0E, which the OBDb repositories for the Honda Accord, CR-V, Civic, Pilot, Ridgeline and ZR-V, among others also use but only the Civic one was archived (https://github.com/OBDb/Honda-Civic/blob/main/signalsets/v3/default.json, archived https://web.archive.org/web/20261115134434/https://github.com/OBDb/Honda-Civic/blob/main/signalsets/v3/default.json), CC-BY-SA-4.0, the address pair only
